countingUnits.impact: PRINTINGS the resolver assigns to the rule this task teaches — a (cardId, variantId) count, since a holo and a reverse of one card resolve differently. It is the sort key: a mask on a card whose group governs 1,600 printings outranks a one-off. `null` means the input needed to size it is not in this bake, NOT zero
countingUnits.noHandMask: a (cardId, scope) mask unit whose winning record has reviewStatus !== "human-authored" — machine output nobody has corrected. Cards with NO mask at all are excluded on purpose: they have no diff.agreement, and agreement is what ranks this section
countingUnits.divergence: 1 − sidecar.diff.agreement (Jaccard) of the machine mask against the era rule it was seeded from. HIGH divergence means the era rule and the machine both had to guess and disagreed, which is exactly where a hand mask teaches the most
countingUnits.emptyPool: an implemented recipe the resolver never picks. The bake's own diagnosis block says WHICH of four causes, and the four imply four different contributions — they are not one backlog
countingUnits.estimate: a TIER, not a number: minutes / half-hour / hours. Every tier carries a one-line rationale. Anything more precise would be invented

skills.mask: Mask drawing — trace where the foil actually sits on one printing.
skills.slider: Slider tuning — move the canon dials until the recipe matches the reference.
skills.glsl: GLSL — write or repair a pattern recipe.
skills.research: Research / citation — find a source that names cards, and cite it.
skills.live-tilt: Live tilt — look at a tilting card and record a verdict. No code. This is a real skill here because the still-frame judge is structurally blind to motion, and a human eye is the only instrument that is not.

guards.do-not-flip-winners: Do not flip a resolver winner just to fill a pool. Cited rows routinely describe different physical layers of the same card — one names the sheet, another names the art window — and both being true is a documented non-bug. Closing this means finding a source the resolver does not have, not re-ranking the ones it does.
guards.live-tilt-not-glsl: The ask here is a LIVE-TILT HUMAN VERDICT, not another GLSL round. This nay is a motion claim, and the judge scores still frames; several of its claims are already refuted at pixel level. Shader work cannot move a dimension the instrument cannot measure.
guards.needs-a-bake: Closing this edits data/foil-card-assignments.json, which changes what the resolver guesses. The verification map and the pattern-card pools this queue is built from are bake outputs, so they must be regenerated in the same change or the queue will describe a corpus that no longer exists.

estimateTiers.minutes: One sitting at one card. Open it, look, answer.
estimateTiers.half-hour: One focused pass over one thing, with the surface already in front of you.
estimateTiers.hours: New work — a recipe, a silhouette from scratch, or a source that has to be found before it can be cited.
